## Data set-up

## PART ONE

## Question 1

```{r}
## Convert date variables to date format then sort the data
ppn_subset_2000 <- ppn_subset_2000 %>%
  mutate(episode_start_date = dmy(episode_start_date),
         episode_end_date = dmy(episode_end_date)) %>%
  arrange(ppn, episode_start_date, episode_end_date)

## Attach labels to mode_of_separation
ppn_subset_2000$mode_of_separation_recode <- factor(ppn_subset_2000$mode_of_separation_recode,
                                                    levels = c(seq(0,11,1)),
                                                    labels = c("Discharge on leave", "Discharge by hospital", 
                                                  "Discharge own risk", "Transfer to nursing home",
                                                  "Transfer to public psychiatric hospital", "Transfer to other hospital",
                                                  "Death with autopsy", "Death without autopsy", 
                                                  "Transfer to other accommodation", "Type change separation",
                                                  "Discharge on leave", "Transfer to palliative care unit/hospice"))

## Create a flag for patients with any admissions related to ischemic heart disease
diag_vars <- paste0("diagnosis_code", c("P", seq(1, 19)))
diag_vars

ihd_codes <- c("I20", "I21", "I22", "I24", "I25")

ppn_subset_2000 <- ppn_subset_2000 %>% 
  mutate(ihd = 1 * if_any(all_of(diag_vars), ~ str_sub(.x, 1, 3) %in% ihd_codes))

## Create a one-way frequency table of ihd to check that flag has been created correctly
ppn_subset_2000 %>% tabyl(ihd)
```

[There should be 15,198 records coded with ischemic heart disease events]{style="color:red;"}\
\

## Question 2

A.  Create a frequency table of *year_sep* against flag variable ihd. How many acute cardiovascular events occurred in 2002?\

```{r}
## Create a variable for year of separation
ppn_subset_2000 <- ppn_subset_2000 %>% mutate(year_sep = year(episode_end_date))

## Frequency table of year_sep against ihd
ppn_subset_2000 %>% 
  tabyl(year_sep, ihd) %>% 
  adorn_percentages(denominator = "row") %>%
  adorn_pct_formatting(digits = 0) %>%
  adorn_ns(position = "front")
```

[1,247 episodes of care related to IHD in 2002 (23% of all episodes of care in 2002)]{style="color:red;"}\
\

B.  Why do we use year of separation rather than year of admission?\
    [We use year of separation, not admission, because that is how records are processed within the hospital morbidity system. That is, each record is coded after separation and classified by financial year based on the date of separation.]{style="color:red;"}\
    \

## Question 3

A.  Create and tabulate *ihd_seq*.

```{r}
## Create IHD seq
ppn_subset_2000 <- ppn_subset_2000 %>%
  group_by(ppn) %>%
  mutate(ihd_cumcount = cumsum(ihd), # cumulative total number of IHD records for each person
         post_ihd = as.numeric(ihd_cumcount > 0)) %>% # Flag records that occur on or after first IHD
  group_by(ppn, post_ihd) %>%
  mutate(ihd_seq = row_number() * post_ihd) %>% # If prior to first IHD, seq = 0, otherwise seq = row number
  ungroup()

## Create table of ihd_seq to check
ppn_subset_2000 %>% tabyl(ihd_seq)

ppn_subset_2000 %>% skim(ihd_seq) # Maximum (p100) is 551
```

\
\

B.  Produce a table containing the number of first hospital admissions with ischemic heart disease event (*ihd_seq* = 1) by year of separation.

```{r}
## Create and save a table of year of separation for first IHD hospital admissions
ihd_year_table_2000 <- ppn_subset_2000 %>%
  filter(ihd_seq == 1) %>%
  tabyl(year_sep) %>%
  as_tibble()

ihd_year_table_2000 %>% filter(year_sep == 2010)
```

\
\

## Question 6

Produce a line graph of the annual number of incident cases of ischemic heart disease events from 2010-2020 based on the three datasets you used above.

```{r}
## Basic line graph
plotdata <- bind_rows(
  ihd_year_table_2000 %>% mutate(start = "2000"), # make start year a character not a number, to force R to recognise it as categorical not continuous
  ihd_year_table_2008 %>% mutate(start = "2008"),
  ihd_year_table_2010 %>% mutate(start = "2010"))

## Quick plot to see trends
ggplot(data = plotdata) +
  geom_line(aes(x = year_sep, y = n, colour = start))

## Nicer looking plot (if interested)
ggplot(data = plotdata, mapping = aes(x = year_sep, y = n)) +
  geom_line(aes(colour = start),
            linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_text(data = plotdata %>% group_by(start) %>% slice(n()),
            aes(label = start, colour = start),
            size = 5, fontface = "bold", hjust = 0, nudge_x = 0.2, nudge_y = c(0, -15, 15)) +
  xlab("") +
  ylab("Number of incident IHD hospitalisations") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(2000, 2020),
                  ylim = c(0, 1000),
                  clip = "off") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 2000:2020,
                     minor_breaks = NULL,
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 1000, 250),
                     minor_breaks = seq(0, 1000, 50),
                     expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("2000" = "forestgreen",
                                 "2008" = "royalblue",
                                 "2010" = "firebrick")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(colour = "black", size = 11), 
        axis.title = element_text(colour = "black", size = 14, face = "bold"), 
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
        axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "grey95", linewidth = 0.7),
        panel.grid.minor = element_line(colour = "grey98", linewidth = 0.1),
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        plot.margin = margin(t = 10, b = 0, l = 5, r = 50))
```

A.  What do you notice about the frequencies compared between the three datasets?\
    [Frequencies are higher when starting the analysis in more recent years. This is because we are incorrectly counting IHD hospitalisations as incident IHD, when in fact there was a historical IHD hospitalisation earlier than the start of our analysis dataset.]{style="color:red;"}\
    \
B.  Do you think a 4-year clearance period would be sufficient for obtaining an accurate estimate of incident cases in 2010? [In the full analysis dataset (2000-2020), the number of incident IHD hospitalisations is initially high (due to the prevalent pool effect) but reaches a steady state after about 7-8 years. A 4-year clearance period would probably not be sufficient to accurately estimate incident IHD hospitalisations.]{style="color:red;"}\
    \

```{r}
# Import data from Github ----
## Read in csv file

## Convert date variables to date format then sort the data
apdc_subset <- apdc_subset %>%

```

## Question 7

Define how you would appropriately construct a study population with all the available hospitalisation data to determine length of stay for their kidney transplant admission. Consider what records should be included. What important assumptions have we made in constructing this study population?

[**Steps for constructing the study population:**]{style="color:red;"}

[1. Determine which episodes of care were part of the same hospital admission.]{style="color:red;"}

[2. Flag any hospital admissions where any diagnosis code within any episode of care was related to kidney transplant]{style="color:red;"}

[3. Remove episodes of care if there was no kidney transplant flagged for the entire hospital admission.]{style="color:red;"}

[4. Calculate length of stay for each hospital admission (latest episode end date minus earliest episode start date).]{style="color:red;"}

[5. Collapse the dataset to one row per person per kidney transplant hospital admission, keeping the length of stay for each admission.]{style="color:red;"}

[**Assumptions:**]{style="color:red;"}

[1. Hospital admissions are for kidney transplant even if the primary diagnosis code was unrelated.]{style="color:red;"}

[2. We are assuming the entire length of stay was attributable to the kidney transplant, and not other medical issues that arose.]{style="color:red;"}

[3. All transfers have been accounted for correctly, and there were no interstate transfers.]{style="color:red;"}\
\

## Question 8

A.  Looking at observations relating to ppn "Ue/R3tAbxDO" and year of separation = 2012. Which episodes of care have overlapping dates and how many total hospital admissions did this person have?

```{r}
## Create a variable for year of separation
apdc_subset <- apdc_subset %>% mutate(year_sep = year(episode_end_date))

## Observations for ppn "Ue/R3tAbxDO" and year of separation 2012
apdc_subset %>%   
  filter(ppn == "Ue/R3tAbxDO" & year_sep==2012) %>%
  select(ppn, episode_start_date, episode_end_date, mode_of_separation_recode) %>% 
  print()

```

[PPN Ue/R3tAbxDO (2012) = 5 episodes, 4 admissions:]{style="color:red;"}

[- #1 and #2 overlap (#1 end date is same as #2 start date). But they are two separate admissions. #1 is a single-day admission, #2 is an entirely new admission]{style="color:red;"}

[- #3 and #4 overlap (#3 end date is same as #4 start date). #3 ends with a transfer, so these are both part of the same admission.]{style="color:red;"}\
\

B.  Looking at observations relating to ppn "7339/kP/Dy2" and year of separation = 2001. Which episodes of care have overlapping dates and how many total hospital admissions did this person have?

```{r}

```

[PPN 7339/kP/Dy2 (2001) = 5 episodes, 3 admissions]{style="color:red;"}

[- #1, #2, and #3 overlap (#1 end date is same as #2 start date, and #2 end date is same as #3 start date)]{style="color:red;"}

[- #1 and #2 ends with a transfer, so #1 and #2 are both part of the same admission.]{style="color:red;"}

C.  Looking at observations relating to ppn "XxhXRhIWyyH" and year of separation = 2010. Which episodes of care have overlapping dates and how many total hospital admissions did this person have?

[- #5, #6, #7, and #8 all overlap (#5 end = #6 start, #6 end = #7 start, and #8 starts and ends in between #7 start and end)]{style="color:red;"}

E.  What further information would be helpful in deciding which transfers align to the same hospital admission?

[It would be helpful to know:]{style="color:red;"}

[- The time of day of each episode start and end, to decide whether episodes of care on the same day that end in discharge are genuinely separate admissions or if this is an error and they should be part of the same admission.]{style="color:red;"}

[- How each episode started (‘mode of admission’) to determine if the patient was transferred from elsewhere or was a new admission.]{style="color:red;"}

[- The hospital where each episode of care took place, and the hospital that the patient was transferred from and to.]{style="color:red;"}\

## Question 9

Define the data processing steps that would be necessary to identify and group together the episodes of care to reflect the same hospitalisation admission.\

[If an episode of care is nested within another episode of care, it must be part of the same admission. We would take the earliest episode start date and latest episode end date to define the admission]{style="color:red;"}

[If an episode starts on the same day that another ends, we would need to check the mode of separation, as well as the facility code, facility transferred from, and facility transferred to. Then we can determine which episode end date would be most appropriate]{style="color:red;"}

[If an episode of care does not have overlapping dates with another episode of care, they are two separate admissions and each episode start date and end date can be used respectively.]{style="color:red;"}\
\

## Question 10

Apply the provided transfers code *transfers()* to add variables to your dataset to identify which episodes of care belong to the same hospital admission. Identify the number of transfers (including type changes):

```{r}
## Load transfers package
library(devtools)
install_github("james-hedley/transfers")
library(transfers)

#Remove labels from mode of separation
apdc_subset$mode_of_separation_recode <- c(0,1,2,4,5,7,8,9)[as.integer(apdc_subset$mode_of_separation_recode)]

## Identify transfers in the analysis dataset
apdc_subset <- apdc_subset %>%
  transfers(id = "ppn",
                admdate = "episode_start_date",
                sepdate = "episode_end_date",
                mode = "mode_of_separation_recode")

```

\
\

## Question 11

Using all the available data in the data set, create a data set containing only records relating to kidney transplant.

```{r}
## Create a flag for patients with any admissions related to kidney transplant
diag_vars <- paste0("diagnosis_code", c("P", seq(1, 19)))
diag_vars

ktx_codes <- c("Z94")

apdc_subset <- apdc_subset %>% 
  mutate(ktx = 1 * if_any(all_of(diag_vars), ~ str_sub(.x, 1, 3) %in% ktx_codes)) %>% 
  group_by(ppn, stayseq) %>% 
  mutate(ktx_adm=max(ktx)) %>% #Flag for all obs of the same admission
  ungroup()

## Create analysis dataset restricted to episodes of care related to kidney transplant
analysis_ktx_data <- apdc_subset %>%
  filter(ktx_adm==1)

```

\
\

## Question 12

Calculate the mean length of stay by:

A.  ignoring transfers (i.e., assume each episode of care is a separate hospital admission, with transfers representing a ‘new’ admission).

```{r}
## Mean LOS ignoring transfers
analysis_ktx_data %>% 
  mutate(los = as.numeric(episode_end_date - episode_start_date)) %>% 
  filter(ktx==1) %>% 
  skim(los)
```

[Ignoring transfers and counting each episode of care: Mean = 3.52 days]{style="color:red;"}\
\

B.  accounting for transfers (i.e., where all episodes of care for a single hospital admission have been linked)

```{r}
## Mean LOS accounting for transfers (count each admission once)
analysis_ktx_data %>%
  group_by(ppn, stayseq) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(los = as.numeric(totlos)) %>%
  skim(los)

```

[Accounting for transfers and counting each admission only once: Mean = 4.41 days]{style="color:red;"}
\

C.  compare these with the mean of the existing APDC variable *episode_length_of_stay*.

```{r}
## Amend episode length of stay for minimum of 1 day
analysis_ktx_data <- analysis_ktx_data %>% 
  mutate(episode_length_of_stay = ifelse(episode_length_of_stay==0, 1, episode_length_of_stay))

## Mean LOS provided
analysis_ktx_data %>%
  skim(episode_length_of_stay)
```

[Using provided episode_length_of_stay and counting each episode of care: Mean = 4.06 days]{style="color:red;"}\
\
